comparison: Both evaluate the core mathematical results (C16-C20) from the branching process model. OpenEval finds the mathematical derivations consistent and well-supported with proofs. Peer reviewers praised the 'elegant modeling' and did not challenge the mathematical framework, though they suggested reorganizing presentation. Strong agreement on validity of theoretical results.

Both address radiographic tumor burden measurements (C30, C31, C57). OpenEval finds the observational data clearly described and appropriate. Peer reviewers did not challenge the data collection itself but requested improved presentation with conversion scales for clinical interpretation, indicating the data was acceptable but presentation needed enhancement.

Both evaluate simultaneous vs sequential therapy findings (C5, C32-C37, C51-C52). OpenEval finds results internally consistent and mathematically sound, with minor concern about 'always' language. Peer reviewers strongly supported these findings, specifically requesting supplementary figure 3 be moved to main text to enhance impact. Strong agreement on this key result.

Both address cancer stem cell implications (C38-C40, C72). OpenEval finds the logic sound with appropriate citations, noting plasticity complicates assumptions. Peer reviewers expressed concern that this important distinction was 'quickly dismissed as not relevant clinically' and requested more commentary since 'the cancer stem cell question remains murky.' Disagreement on adequacy of treatment of this topic.

Both evaluate discussion of immunotherapy limitations (C48-C50, C76). OpenEval finds the acknowledgment of model limitations appropriate and scientifically humble. Peer reviewers found this discussion insufficient, explicitly requesting more detailed commentary on how modeling applies to immunotherapy responses. Disagreement on adequacy of immunotherapy discussion.

Both address empirical dataset and parameter estimation (C12-C15, C58, C21). OpenEval validates parameters against literature and finds calculations well-documented. Peer reviewers raised significant concerns about generalizability from BRAF mutant melanoma to all cancers and challenged the 7-day doubling assumption, requesting sensitivity analysis. Disagreement on parameter validity and generalizability.

Both evaluate dual therapy predictions (C3, C25-C28, C44). OpenEval finds calculations internally consistent following from equation (1). Peer reviewers found this 'an important contribution based on elegant modeling work' without challenging core findings. Strong agreement on these predictions, though OpenEval notes C44 may overstate certainty.

Both address triple therapy predictions (C29, C45, with C4 also in peer evaluation). OpenEval finds the extension to triple therapy mathematically consistent with the model framework. Peer reviewers did not question these findings, with overall favorable evaluation suggesting acceptance. Agreement on triple therapy conclusions.

Both evaluate the mathematical modeling framework (C53-C55, C59-C60, plus additional claims in OpenEval). OpenEval finds the model appropriately grounded in established theory with extensive validation. Peer reviewers requested clarification on how the model differs from previous work and expressed concern about handling spatial structure and non-homogeneous growth in solid tumors. Disagreement on adequacy of methodological justification.

Both address clinical recommendations about cross-resistance (C74-C75, plus C46-C47 in OpenEval). OpenEval finds recommendations logical based on model predictions, noting C75 is somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers did not challenge these therapeutic implications. Agreement on clinical recommendations derived from modeling.

Both address parameter sensitivity (C71, C73, C79 in OpenEval; broader sensitivity concerns in peer review). OpenEval finds identification of key parameters follows logically from mathematical formulas with supporting sensitivity analysis. Peer reviewers explicitly requested more thorough sensitivity analysis, asking how predictions would change with different parameter values. Disagreement on adequacy of sensitivity analysis.

Partial overlap on costly resistance scenarios (C69-C70). OpenEval finds simulation results consistent with expectations about fitness costs. Peer reviewers' concern about parameter sensitivity (point 5) extends to these predictions, questioning robustness to parameter variations. Disagreement on confidence in parameter-dependent predictions.

Both address primary conclusions about dual therapy necessity (C3-C4). OpenEval expresses uncertainty due to critical dependence on no cross-resistance assumption (n12=0), noting the model fails when cross-resistance exists. Peer reviewers found the paper an important contribution and did not challenge these core findings. Disagreement on certainty of main conclusions given model assumptions.

Minimal overlap on empirical parameter estimation (C21 shared). OpenEval finds median decline rate directly calculated from observed data. Peer reviewers' broader concerns about parameter validity and generalizability (point 3) extend to all empirical parameters. Partial disagreement on parameter robustness.

Both address high-turnover tumor predictions (C79). OpenEval finds this demonstrates appropriate model sensitivity to birth rate parameters. Peer reviewers' request for more sensitivity analysis (point 5) indicates uncertainty about how robust such predictions are to parameter variations. Disagreement on confidence in parameter-sensitive predictions.

OpenEval evaluated claims about treatment mechanism timing (C42-C43), finding the conclusion about minor differences between mechanisms supported by calculations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval evaluated background claims about targeted therapy resistance (C1, C6-C11), finding them well-documented with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - reviewers did not comment on background/introduction claims.

OpenEval evaluated the rationale for combination therapy (C2) as established scientific consensus. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - reviewers did not comment on this foundational claim.

OpenEval evaluated simulation results predicting universal monotherapy failure (C22-C24), finding them consistent with model and clinical experience. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific simulation results.
